metadata.value: Plain integer triples sorted in permutations SPO, POS, OSP, OPS
metadata.normalized_value: Plain integer triples sorted in permutations SPO, POS, OSP, OPS
metadata.evidence: The library works exclusively with integer triples, thus the data has to be prepared accordingly prior to indexing and querying. We assume the RDF triples have been mapped to integer identifiers and sorted in different permutations of the subject (S), predicate (P) and object (O) components.
metadata.reason: Defines the input data format.

metadata.evidence:
-  `RDF_dataset.spo`
-  `RDF_dataset.pos`
-  `RDF_dataset.osp`
-  `RDF_dataset.ops`
metadata.reason: Necessary input files for indexing.

metadata.value: Plain text file with 7 integers (total triples, distinct subjects, distinct predicates, distinct objects, distinct S-P pairs, distinct P-O pairs, distinct O-S pairs)
metadata.normalized_value: Plain text file with 7 integers (total triples, distinct subjects, distinct predicates, distinct objects, distinct S-P pairs, distinct P-O pairs, distinct O-S pairs)
metadata.evidence:
We also need a metadata file contaning some useful statistics about the data. This file must be named `RDF_dataset.stats`. Also this file is in plain format and contains 7 integers, one per line:

1. total number of triples
2. distinct subjects
3. distinct predicates
4. distinct objects
5. distinct S-P pairs
6. distinct P-O pairs
7. distinct O-S pairs
metadata.reason: Describes the statistics metadata file.
